successors.name: British Cape Colony
successors.text: Gcalekaland and the Xhosa-speaking chiefdoms east of the Great Kei: 'Gcalekaland, the last independent Xhosa state'; the box (Great Kei to the Mthatha, Pondoland's southern edge) is the researcher's…

ledger.x: 1779: the Fish River becomes the Cape-Xhosa line.
1812 (bridge): Colonel Graham's force drives the Xhosa back beyond the Fish River.
December 1836: Queen Adelaide Province is given back.
1878: the end of the last independent Xhosa state (Ninth War).

wars.name: Zuurveld war
wars.outcome: Colonel Graham drives the Xhosa back beyond the Fish River.

wars.name: Sixth Xhosa War
wars.outcome: Hintsa killed in 1835; the Keiskamma-Kei country annexed as Queen Adelaide Province, then given back in December 1836.

wars.name: Seventh Xhosa War
wars.outcome: 'King Sandile kaNgqika led the Ngqika people in the Seventh Frontier War (1846-47)'; British Kaffraria is annexed in 1847.

wars.name: Eighth Xhosa War
wars.outcome: 'It lasted over two years and ended in the complete subjugation of the Ciskei Xhosa.'

wars.name: Ninth Xhosa War
wars.outcome: 'A final blow for the last independent Xhosa state, Gcalekaland'; Sarhili applied for peace; Gcalekaland administered as a British territory.

certainty.note: Only the Fish (1779), Keiskamma (1819-20) and Great Kei (1835, 1847) lines are on the pages; the east is a researcher-drawn box.
